# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives me the core secret: the light walks a circle of five colours, and the cut depends on the light at the cut moment — green→cut yellow, orange→cut blue, yellow→cut green. Three rows only; two circle colours are unmapped, so nobody cuts until we know more or get more manual pages.

My only channel is gestures to Deaf. Deaf can see the bomb, and Deaf can speak — so Deaf is the bridge: they read my tokens, ask questions out loud (I can hear, I just can't talk back), and I answer with 👍/👎. Blind then works the bomb on Deaf's spoken word.

Problem: no gesture means anything yet. I can't explain a code, so I'll propose one and let Deaf interrogate me. I'll open with three identical gestures to signal "three of something" (the table has three pairs), then send three two-gesture pairs. I've built in a tell for structure: two tokens recur across pairs — ✋ and ✌ each appear twice, once first and once second — exactly what a colour table looks like (yellow is both a light and a cut colour, same for green). Deaf sees the bomb's actual colours and wires, so their verbal guesses next round should land close, and I'll confirm or reject each one.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: This is the blind one. Under my fingers the bomb has one display, one light, and three wire positions numbered 1 to 3. Cutting a wire is the only action I have. I cannot read the display and colour never reaches me. I never see gestures, so I receive nothing from your hands and nothing from the deaf one's hands. My only ears are the deaf one's voice, and their words reach me one round after they are spoken. So please relay the manual to the deaf one by gesture, and have them speak every relevant rule aloud to me: anything about the wires, the display, and the light, and which wire to cut in which case. To the deaf one I just signed a wave, then an open palm raised toward them meaning speak to me, then three fingers meaning three wires. I will not cut anything until I have instructions.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, this is Deaf. I saw your four gesture groups but cannot decode them yet. Let us fix one code. I will now show you five gestures in order; they mean, in order: one, two, three, five, zero. Use finger count for any number: wire numbers, counts of things. Also: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no. Bomb report: display shows zero. Indicator light is yellow. Wire one is yellow, wire two is green, wire three is blue. Tell me which module the manual makes of this and what must be done. Echo the code back to confirm you understood, then give me the instruction. I will speak it to Blind for you.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✊]

What I learned this round: Deaf fixed a numeric code with me — ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5, ✊=0, 👍/👎 = yes/no — and reported the bomb: display zero, light yellow, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Blind confirmed they can only hear Deaf's voice, one round late, and will not touch anything until instructed. So Deaf is the only bridge to Blind, and my gestures are the only bridge to Deaf.

What the bomb is, per my manual: a light-gated cut. The light walks a five-colour circle, changing every round, and the wire must match the light shown at the moment of the cut. Right now (yellow light) wire 2 would be correct — but the light moves every round, and Deaf's words only reach Blind a round after being spoken. So a one-time answer is useless and dangerous; we need the cycle predicted one step ahead. Blind should hold until Deaf has watched several rounds, fixed the circle's order, and can command "next round the light will be X, cut wire Y" — and nobody ever cuts when the light shows one of the two colours my table doesn't map.

What I'm sending: the requested echo plus 👍 to lock the code; "three"; then three (light-reference, cut-wire) pairs. I reference light colours by the wire sharing that colour — [✌ ☝] = "light has wire 2's colour (green) → cut wire 1", [☝ ✌] = "light has wire 1's colour (yellow) → cut wire 2". Orange has no wire, so I mark it with a fresh token 🤏 and let Deaf name candidate colours aloud next round; I answer with 👍/👎 — that yes/no channel over Deaf's voice is our reliable decoder. The trailing ✊ means zero cuts until the protocol is confirmed. My pairs are deliberately decodable (Deaf knows the wire colours they reported), and anything misread gets filtered by Deaf's spoken questions before anyone touches a wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
```

Question two: I read your last message as: yellow light, cut two then one; red light, pinch-cut three; another color, one then two. Right or wrong: 👍 or 👎. Question three: does 🤏 mean cut or snip? 👍 or 👎. If no option fits, send ✋ and we will build a spelling code. From now on a lone ✊ means end of message.

What I learned: the light has now shown RED — a colour my manual's table does not contain (it maps only green, orange, yellow). So red is one of the two unmapped circle colours, and the correct action under red is no cut at all. Deaf also misread my table as double cuts ("cut two then one"), which is dangerously wrong: each rule is exactly ONE cut, conditioned on the light colour at the cut moment. And Blind cannot perceive the light, so Deaf — the only one who sees it — must eventually predict the next round's colour and command accordingly, since their voice reaches Blind one round late.

My answers, in Deaf's asked order: Q1 → zero (✊): with a red light, nothing in the manual authorizes any cut. Q2 → 👎: the reading was wrong. Q3 → 👎: 🤏 is not an action at all — it marks a light colour, and critically it is NOT the red Deaf just saw; that's exactly the confusion that could kill us. My Q1 answer (red → no cut) already contradicts the table row "🤏 → cut 3," so Deaf can deduce by elimination: 🤏 is neither red, nor yellow/green/blue (those are referenced by wires 1/2/3) — it is the fifth colour, which Deaf will see and can name when the light walks to it.

I resend the rules with a constant ✋ prefix marking "when the light is…": first symbol = light colour (referenced by the wire sharing that colour; 🤏 for the no-wire colour), second symbol = the one wire to cut. So: green light → wire 1, 🤏 light → wire 3, yellow light → wire 2. Then 🖐 seeds the fact Deaf lacks from my manual: the circle has five colours — three mapped, red and one other unmapped, and an unmapped light always means no cut. Nobody cuts until Deaf has echoed this table back and I have confirmed it, and until the full five-colour cycle has been observed so commands can be predicted one round ahead.
